thesis: Virgin Galactic is a pre-revenue commercial spaceflight company whose entire equity value hinges on one binary catalyst: the Delta-class spaceship program. Prototype VSS Unity has returned to flight to de-risk the new vehicle, glide/flight tests of the first Delta ship are guided for Q3 2026, rocket-powered spaceflights for Q4 2026, and private-astronaut commercial service ramps from January 2027 toward 8-plus flights per month by mid-2027. Management guides roughly $450M annual revenue and $100M adjusted EBITDA at fleet scale. Against that, FY2025 revenue was just $1.54M on a $278.9M net loss, the company continues to burn cash and dilute shareholders (debt-for-equity swaps and a fresh mixed-securities shelf), and ~40% of the float is sold short. This is a pure speculative call option on Delta-class execution.

drivers: First Delta-class ship completes Q3 2026 flight tests and Q4 2026 rocket-powered spaceflight on schedule
Commercial private-astronaut service begins January 2027 and ramps toward 8-plus flights per month by Q2 2027
Second Delta-class ship enters service late Q4 2026 / early Q1 2027, unlocking the $450M revenue and $100M adjusted EBITDA target at fleet scale
Backlog of ~650 existing ticket holders and higher seat pricing validate suborbital tourism demand

base_case.assumptions: Delta-class flight tests broadly hold to schedule but commercial ramp slips into 2027 with only one ship operating most of the year. Revenue remains modest through 2027 and one or more dilutive capital raises are needed off the new shelf. Stock trades around the analyst consensus target ($3.43–$3.52) as investors wait for proof of sustained commercial cadence.

risks: Delta-class encounters significant technical delays or a failure during flight test
Cash runway tightens through 2027; distressed financing or a strategic review is required
Further shareholder dilution of 30%+ via equity issuance under the mixed-securities shelf
Suborbital tourism demand disappoints at the higher post-relaunch seat price

catalysts.event: Glide and flight tests of the first Delta-class SpaceShip
First rocket-powered Delta-class spaceflight and limited commercial service launch
Second Delta-class ship expected to enter service
Private-astronaut commercial flights begin (~4 per month), ramping to 8-plus per month by Q2 2027

key_risks: Delta-class program delays or a technical failure during flight test
Persistent cash burn and reliance on dilutive raises under the new mixed-securities shelf
Elevated short interest (~40% of float) amplifies volatility
Competition from Blue Origin (New Shepard) and the newly public SpaceX (SPCX)
Luxury discretionary spending vulnerability in recessions
FAA Part 450 licensing required before the first powered Delta mission
